children: Snabbit reported a net loss of Rs 168 crore in FY26 on operating revenue of Rs 12.25 crore, as the two-year-old on-demand home services startup invested in customer acquisition, workforce expansion and service delivery amid intensifying competition in the quick home services market, as per a media report.

The company’s operating revenue increased from Rs 26 lakh in FY25 to Rs 12.25 crore in FY26, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). However, its total expenses rose sharply to Rs 195 crore from Rs 6.8 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Founded in 2024 by Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit connects households with trained professionals for tasks such as cleaning, dishwashing and laundry. Customers can book services by the hour, with the platform offering fulfilment within 10 minutes.

Platform services generated Rs 10.82 crore, accounting for 88 per cent of operating revenue in FY26. The remaining revenue came from uniform sales. The company also reported Rs 14.76 crore in other income, primarily from interest earned on bank deposits.

Snabbit’s expenditure included Rs 46 crore in employee benefit costs and Rs 63 crore in expert service costs. It spent another Rs 49 crore on marketing and Rs 23.8 crore on service fulfilment. Banking charges, commissions, recruitment, legal expenses, software maintenance and other overheads contributed to total expenses of Rs 195 crore.
The company’s net loss widened from Rs 5.7 crore in FY25 to Rs 168 crore in FY26. At the unit level, Snabbit spent Rs 15.92 to generate every rupee of operating revenue.
Its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -58.45 per cent, while its EBITDA margin was -1,481.63 per cent in FY26.
Snabbit has raised more than USD 112 million to date. Its funding includes a USD 56 million Series D round backed by Susquehanna VC, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments.

The startup has also reported growth in service volumes. It said it crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a single day and completed four million home-help jobs during Q1 FY27. Its burn per job declined by more than Rs 100 quarter-on-quarter to below Rs 250.

Agarwal said FY26 was the company’s first full year of operations. During the year, Snabbit expanded from around 500 daily jobs across eight micro-markets to 35,000 daily jobs across more than 100 micro-markets, representing a 75-fold increase in daily jobs. It also acquired nearly one million customers and onboarded more than 20,000 experts.

The founder attributed the Rs 167.8 crore loss to investments in expansion, customer and expert acquisition, and long-term capabilities. He said FY26 financials do not reflect current economics, pointing to improvements in operating leverage and unit economics as the business built greater density across neighbourhoods.

Snabbit is competing with Urban Company’s InstaHelp and Pronto, as companies seek to build demand for on-demand household services. Urban Company’s InstaHelp completed around 1.9 million orders in July 2026, ahead of Snabbit’s 1.85 million, while Pronto crossed 1.25 million bookings.
Urban Company has also been investing in its quick home services business and has reportedly been looking to raise USD 200 million, as competition in the segment intensifies.

The companies are expanding their customer bases, building workforces and increasing fulfilment capacity. However, their ability to translate higher order volumes into sustainable earnings will depend on worker utilisation, customer acquisition costs, repeat bookings and the density of demand within individual neighbourhoods.

For Snabbit and its competitors, the challenge is to establish a business model in which bookings generate sufficient revenue to cover service delivery and operating costs. Until then, continued expansion may require further funding as the companies work towards improving unit economics.
